source_caption:
How High is a stoner comedy starring rappers Method Man and Redman as two underachieving friends, Silas and Jamal. After smoking marijuana grown with the ashes of a deceased friend, they realize they can see his ghost, who helps them cheat on an important college entrance exam. Surprisingly, they score high enough to get accepted into Harvard University.

At Harvard, the duo struggle to fit into the elite academic environment but use their ghostly helper to pass exams and navigate challenges. The film mixes absurd humor with themes of friendship and ambition, while poking fun at Ivy League stereotypes. Though it received mixed reviews from critics, it became a cult favorite among fans of early 2000s comedy.

source_details.title: How High
source_details.synopsis: How High is a 2001 American stoner comedy film directed by Jesse Dylan in his feature directorial debut and written by Dustin Lee Abraham. The film stars Method Man and Redman as two cannabis users who gain admission to Harvard University with the supernatural help of a deceased friend whose ashes were used to fertilize a marijuana plant. Obba Babatundé, Mike Epps, Jeffrey Jones, and Fred Willard also appear in supporting roles. Produced by Jersey Films and Native Pictures and distributed by Universal Pictures, How High was released on December 21, 2001. The film received generally negative reviews from critics, but later gained a cult following. A television sequel, How High 2, was released
